Crystal Clear icons

Everaldo Coelho’s glossy, translucent desktop icons: saturated color, bright highlights, and soft shading.

Context

Coelho’s “crystal” look “consists of icons that appear to be made of highly reflective surfaces.” He aimed “between realism of Mac OS X and cartoon colored style of XP.” Crystal SVG became KDE’s default icon theme in KDE 3.1; the later Crystal Clear set made icons appear transparent. Wikipedia: Everaldo Coelho.

The Wikipedia Frutiger Aero article illustrates “vibrant colors, three-dimensional graphics, and glossy textures” with this icon, and lists Crystal icons under “See also.” Wikipedia: Frutiger Aero.

Observed

  • Three rounded, faceless figures in saturated green, blue, and red look like molded gel.
  • Each figure has a bright white specular highlight on the head and shoulder and darker shading at the edges.
  • A yellow warning triangle with an exclamation mark overlaps the front, with a soft shadow.

Why it belongs

Crystal predates Vista, but it already has the style’s icon grammar: candy color, gel volume, and a single hard highlight. It helped make gloss the default look of free desktops.

Borrow

Draw icons as simple rounded volumes with one strong white highlight and a darker rim, rather than outlines.
